title: The New Era of Wikimedia Traffic: Thinking Beyond Pageviews
content:
Part 1 of Wikimedia in a Changing Traffic Ecosystem: This post begins a series for Wikimedia communities, and other interested readers, exploring some recent readership trends and what they mean for the movement’s future. Drawing on research from across the Wikimedia Foundation, we’ll examine the forces shaping our traffic, the implications for readers and contributors, and how these findings can inform our strategy.

For more than two decades, billions of visits to Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects have reflected something remarkable: people around the world choose to seek out, share, and contribute to free, human knowledge. Pageviews have long been one of Wikimedia’s most important measures of readership, helping us understand how people access and engage with our projects.

title: Navigating WikiIndaba 2026 Hackathon
content:
Have you ever looked forward to a hackathon so much that you started planning your contributions even before it began? You attended the info session, listened to the project introductions and you can already picture yourself contributing to two or three tools. The excitement is there, the adrenaline building, even confident enough to ask the organisers if one can contribute to more than one tool.

That was me ahead of the WikiIndaba 2026 hackathon but there was one thing I did not factor into my plans: my internet connection. My network had its own plans that it was not interested in my three-tool ambition. What followed was a weekend of trying different workspaces, adjusting expectations, unexpected connections and eventually finding my place in a team.

title: Beyond WikiCamp: Reuniting for an Adventure
content:
For the winning teams of Wikimedia Armenia’s Summer Youth WikiCamp 2026, the adventure didn’t end with the closing ceremony. As a reward for their achievements in Wikipedia editing, sports, intellectual games, and cultural activities during the camp (August 9–16), the two winning teams earned something special: an excursion to a destination of their choice. The excursion is a traditional part of Wikimedia Armenia’s Summer Youth WikiCamp, giving the most active participants an opportunity to continue their camp experience beyond the editing sessions and activities. Each year, the winning teams get to choose their preferred destination, turning their achievements into an opportunity to discover Armenia, explore its cultural and natural heritage, and create memories together.

After voting on the options, the campers chose to explore Syunik, one of Armenia’s most picturesque regions, with an itinerary featuring Shaki Waterfall, Tatev Monastery, Goris, and Old Khndzoresk. Given the distance and number of places to discover, the trip included an overnight stay in Goris.

title: Building Bridges, Empowering Leaders, and Expanding Open Knowledge: My Experience at the Wikimedia Train the Trainer Leadership Workshop in Abuja
content:
In September 2026, I had the privilege of participating in the Wikimedia Leadership Workshop Training, tagged “Train the Trainer,” held at the Exclusive Serene Hotel, Abuja, Nigeria, and hosted by the Wikimedia User Group Nigeria.

The workshop brought together passionate Wikimedia leaders, community organisers, trainers, and knowledge advocates from different states across North Central Nigeria. It was more than a training programme; it was an opportunity to connect, learn, exchange ideas, share experiences, and explore practical ways of strengthening the Wikimedia movement and expanding access to free and open knowledge.

I was particularly honoured to represent the leadership voices and interests of North Central Nigeria, joining fellow leaders from other zones to contribute to conversations around community development, leadership, capacity building, knowledge sharing, and the future of the Wikimedia movement in Nigeria.

title: Wikimedia Armenia’s Contribution to Environmental Awareness Through the “Wikipedia for Green Innovation” Project
content:
As discussions on biodiversity, climate change, and sustainable development gain increasing importance worldwide, access to reliable knowledge about green solutions is more important than ever. In October 2026, against the backdrop of the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity held in Yerevan, Armenia, Wikimedia Armenia and the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom joined forces to organize “Wikipedia for Green Innovation” – an initiative aimed at expanding Armenian Wikipedia’s coverage of green innovation, renewable energy, circular economy, sustainable technologies, and related topics.

The project brought together newcomers and experienced Wikimedians, encouraging them to turn knowledge into freely accessible content. Out of 130 applicants, 65 were newcomers. Wikimedia Armenia organized online and offline training sessions from September 30 to October 18, introducing new participants to Wikipedia’s editing principles, article creation, reliable sourcing, and citation practices.

title: Whose Knowledge Gets Counted? Fourteen Years of Wikidata and African Women’s Contributions
content:
For fourteen years, Wikidata has helped organise the world’s knowledge into a structured, interconnected and freely accessible resource. From people and institutions to languages, cultural heritage and historical events, its data connects information across languages and digital platforms.

Yet, as Wikidata celebrates its 14th birthday and enters its fifteenth year, an important question remains: whose knowledge is being documented, whose contributions are visible, and who gets to participate in shaping the knowledge systems increasingly influencing how we discover and understand the world?

For African Wiki Women, this question goes beyond the absence of biographies or incomplete records. It concerns their participation in the processes through which knowledge is sourced, organised, connected and made accessible.

title: From a rejected applicant to the Mentor Summit: Wikimedia at Google Summer of Code 2026
content:
📷 Featured image: GSoC Mentor Summit 2026 group photo

In 2018, I applied to Google Summer of Code but wasn’t selected. The next year I reapplied and got selected as a GSoC contributor. I then continued my role as a contributor and mentor and now I have gone on to be Wikimedia’s organisation administrator and then I have represented Wikimedia at GSoC Mentor Summit.

My first summit experience was in 2023, and after some change of plans I had the privilege of returning to my second in Munich, Germany. From 30 October – 1 November 2026, I joined Sarthak Parashar as one of two representatives to meet mentors and org admins of more than 100 open source communities.

All below is a summary of what we discussed, what other communities are facing and what I think should be brought back to Wikimedia.

This is unlike any conference. As a full unconference, there isn’t a set programme in advance. Any mentor or org admin can submit a session by adding a sticky note to the schedule board and the rest of us choose what sessions to attend. We filled the entire schedule by the first morning, which shows what’s currently on people’s minds.

title: Wiki for Human Rights Nigeria: Wiki Leadership Training, Electoral Integrity Training, End-of-Year Fiscal Meeting, and October Physical Meetup
content: From August to September, I participated in the WLX Initiative programme organized by Wikimedia Nigeria and a Nigerian consulting firm, Knewrow. When I was selected to be part of the programme, I knew it was a four-week programme, but I didn’t know what it entailed until I became involved in the series of virtual sessions, assignments, and projects. Out of more than 50 participants, I emerged as one of the top five, behind the overall winner, who received a scholarship to Wiki Indaba. The four-week programme leaned heavily on leadership learning moments and reflections. The virtual sessions covered topics on leadership beyond contribution, personal accountability and ownership, communication and community engagement, mentorship and leadership replication, sustainability, social responsibility and community growth, and collaboration and conflict resolution.

title: Preserving Irra’s Heritage, Empowering Its Youth: AIHI and Yoruba Wikipedia Fan Club Offa Train Community Youths Ahead of Oya Festival 2026
content:
The preservation of our cultural heritage begins with the people who own the stories, traditions, and histories. As communities continue to embrace digital technologies, it is increasingly important to equip young people with the knowledge and skills to document, preserve, and share their cultural heritage with the world.

In a significant step towards achieving this, the African Institute for Heritage Intelligence (AIHI), in collaboration with Yoruba Wikipedia Fan Club Offa, organised a one-day digital heritage documentation and Wikimedia training for youths and students in Irra community, ahead of the highly anticipated Oya Festival 2026.

The training was held at the Onira Palace, Irra, providing an important cultural setting for the engagement. Bringing the training to the palace was particularly meaningful, as it connected the younger generation directly with the traditional institution and the cultural heritage they are being empowered to document and preserve.

title: Along the Red Sea Coast: Documenting the Heritage of Hurghada and El Qoseir
content:
From 10 to 12 October 2026, six members of the Egypt Wikimedians User Group embarked on a three-day photo documentation trip to Hurghada and El Qoseir, two coastal cities whose heritage extends far beyond their familiar image as tourist destinations. The expedition explored historic neighbourhoods, museums, scientific institutions, religious landmarks, and industrial remains, documenting the region’s diverse cultural and natural heritage. Through photography and subsequent editorial work, the participants sought to address gaps in the representation of these places across Wikimedia projects and make the history of these places more accessible through freely available knowledge.


The first two days focused on Hurghada, a city shaped by its relationship with the Red Sea, its maritime environment, and the growth of tourism. Rather than focusing solely on its resorts and beaches, the six participants explored several aspects of the city’s urban, cultural, and scientific heritage. The participants were Amr Fathy, Donia El Domiaty, Sohila El Shaer, Summer Kamal, Mohamed Ouda, and Ibrahim El Aidy.
